I ask the question again: What is going on? Why is version a different from version 6? Why are there documents mentioned in version b that are not mentioned in version at Which is the true version or is there going to be a version c?

speakeroldname: Mr. Lee Richardson (Parliamentary Secretary to Minister of Transport):
speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Transport
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, in releasing the report of the deputy ministers on May 14, which provided a chronology of events, every effort was made to provide as complete a record as possible concerning the arrival of Mr. Al-Mashat in Canada on the basis of information then available.
The question of differences between the report released on May 14 and the chronology tabled at the committee on May 30 was referred to by the Secretary of State for External Affairs at the Standing Committee meeting of May 30. At that time she responded that minor differences between the two documents were easily explained by a closer examination of events as time permitted and the coming forward of private citizens to reveal their involvement.
In particular, this resulted in clarification of some points regarding the source and timing of representations on Mr. Al-Mashat's behalf. It also allowed for further amplification of the information on the record.
The matter is still under examination before the standing committee where the government is making every effort to provide a complete and accurate account of the Al-Mashat case.
With regard to the particulars of the memorandum prepared for the Minister of Employment and Immigration, officials of that department will be appearing before the standing committee tomorrow.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Liberal Party
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, tonight I want to follow up on the question I raised on May 28, 1991, concerning the economy in the Gaspe and Magdalen Islands area.
The area, Mr. Speaker, is undoubtedly in deep economic trouble, its youths are discouraged and demoralized because the unemployment rate in Gaspe and the Magdalen Islands is over 27 per cent a figure matched in Canada only by one area in Newfoundland. If there is no change, the whole province of Quebec will soon have this record. That is why the level of self-confidence of the Gaspe people is at its lowest. These people wonder what the future holds for their children in terms of job opportunities.
We must avoid or prevent an exodus of residents in search of lasting jobs they cannot find in their region. Such an exodus, that we must prevent, explains why I raised the issue of the Gaspe economy last May 28.
I asked the Minister of National Health and Welfare when his government would table economic policies that would give some hope and create employment for these people, so that they can work and raise their children in one of the most beautiful regions in Canada.
The minister did not answer my question. Instead, he told me to wait for an announcement he was going to make on his trip to the Gaspe region, on May 30. I listened carefully to what he said, and I must say I am very disappointed with the empty shell the minister unveiled to the people of the Gaspe region. He did not unveil a long-term plan to create long-lasting jobs. Instead, he chose to announce the creation of an Economic Development Agency for that region. The new Agency will receive a $1.7 million subsidy, over the next five years, from the federal minister of Quebec Economic Regional Development. The subsidy will cover the Agency's operational costs. Mr. Speaker, that may look like a considerable amount of money, but over five years, it only means $340,000 a year.
Does the minister really think this Agency will be able to promote the economic and industrial development of this region, as well as attract new investors, with only $340,000? Surely he must be dreaming. But the worst of it is that this subsidy is not new money. That amount had already been allocated by the Conservatives, before the last election, under the 1988 Canada-Quebec Agreement. Is it another election commitment? An old commitment with a new look? We do not know. I remember that, in 1988, before the election, they announced a Canada-Quebec Region Development Agreement worth $800 million.
June 3, 1991

After almost three years, Mr. Speaker, they are still left with $1.7 million to invest in the area where they did nothing since 1988. Are they recycling those promises? Are these new promises? It is definitely not fresh money and the Gaspe people are disappointed by this announcement, by this empty shell. They have not only put forward an empty shell, they have provoked everybody, every circle in Quebec have been incensed by this announcement.
So, Mr. Speaker, I hope the parliamentary secretary will be able to provide me with more concrete answers than the ones the Minister gave me, either in this House or by his announcement.

speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, it is with great pleasure that I will give some information to my hon. colleague. Gaspesie is a region I am particularly fond of. I was bom there and I still have relatives on my father's and my mother's side living there, more precisely in the area of Sainte-Anne-des-Monts, Riviere-Madeleine and other villages in the same county.
Mr. Speaker, I would like to remind the hon. member for Saint-Leonard that the Minister of National Health and Welfare said in this House last week that people in Gaspesie and iles-de-la-Madeleine would be quite happy with the announcements that would be made in the next few days.
Mr. Speaker, if the hon. member and other members of this House read the documents prepared for the visit of the minister in Eastern Quebec, they know that the Minister did not announce only one measure but a whole series of concrete initiatives to promote development and job creation in that region.
The first concerns the creation of the Societe de developpement economique de la Gaspesie et des Iles-de-
Adjoumment Debate
la-Madeleine. This agency will strive to develop the region, it will be active in economic prospecting, investment and promotion of industry and tourism in Canada and abroad.
Mr. Speaker, the government will support the operating costs of this agency for five years, by giving it $1.7 million in financial assistance. The Canadian government will also give $2 million in contribution to the new agency, so that it can take part, as a limited partner, in the new venture capital corporation called Investisse-ment-Gaspesie-Les Iles-de-la-Madeleine Enr.
The minister also announced, Mr. Speaker, the creation of a new loan insurance program which will apply specifically to the Gaspe and Magdalen Island area. With this program, important initiatives will be realized in the area initiatives which would not otherwise get started for want of adequate financing.
I would like to add, Mr. Speaker, that, under this program, our government will be able to offer loan guarantees totalling $6.4 million for the period up to March 31, 1993.
Finally, Mr. Speaker, last week, the hon. minister had the pleasure to announce the extension of the industrial component of the business development program. The objective of this initiative is to make new activities related to the primary and tertiary sectors eligible for federal financial assistance.
If my hon. colleague calls that an empty shell, Mr. Speaker, I personally think that it is very substantial.
